_comment: Antelope Zen Go Synergy Core -- reverse-engineered from USBPcap captures (Windows, VM) in sidejob/zen_go_synergy_core-filtered/ (2026-08-31), cross-checked against the zen-go-tui protocol audit and fixtures. SAME HID vendor protocol family as Orion Studio III (profiles/orion_studio_sc.json) and Discrete 8 Pro: magic 0x70 command, opcode @4, param_id @16, 320-byte reports on the same endpoints. Param IDs are largely shared with Orion; report magics and some frame shapes DIFFER (meter is 0x83 not 0x75; the mixer frame is opcode 0x16 / subcmd 0x04 with no send byte). Everything here is from observed traffic on hardware the capture owner controls. Fields carry status + evidence; anything marked 'observed' is not yet decoded. The official Antelope schema is intentionally not overlaid where it conflicts with this capture-derived Zen Go dialect.

device.name: Antelope Zen Go Synergy Core
device.notes: USB-C bus-powered 4-in / 8-out desktop interface, 2 mic/line/Hi-Z preamps, Synergy Core DSP. Composite device: UAC2 audio (interfaces 0/1/2, 16 in / 16 out, 24-bit, iso endpoints 0x05 OUT / 0x84 IN) plus a vendor HID control interface (interface 3). Device descriptor: class 0xef/0x02/0x01, bcdUSB 0x0200, iManufacturer/iProduct/iSerial 1/2/3. Config descriptor: 4 interfaces, bus-powered (bmAttributes 0x80), maxpower 500 mA.
device.evidence: capture_01_enumeration.pcapng: device descriptor frame -> idVendor 0x23e5, idProduct 0xa015, bcdDevice 0x0606; config descriptor (243 bytes) decoded. The connect-time 0x75 frame carrying ASCII 'Zen Go Synergy Core' + serial + fw rev is a readback RESPONSE for category 0x01 -- see frame.readback, not a Zen-Go-specific name report.

transport.notes: Identical transport to Orion Studio III / Discrete 8 Pro: HID interface 3, interrupt EP 0x01 OUT / 0x82 IN, 320-byte reports, bInterval 6. The HID report descriptor was not captured (the GET_DESCRIPTOR(0x22) request is outside the trace window); the Discrete 8 Pro's is 54 bytes with one 320B Input + one 320B Output report and NO Feature report -- assume the same here until dumped from Linux hidraw (tools/hid_probe.py). If it has no Report ID, Linux hidraw writes need a leading 0x00 (321 bytes) -- see family_notes.
transport.evidence: capture_01_enumeration.pcapng config descriptor: interface 3 = HID, HID desc bcdHID 0x0111 / report desc type 0x22 len 54, EP 0x82 IN + EP 0x01 OUT both interrupt maxpacket 0x0140 (320) bInterval 6.

frame._comment: Outgoing command frames: magic 0x70 @0 (cosmetic in this family), opcode @4, param_id @16. Layout after @16 depends on the opcode.

command.notes: The per-channel / per-bus setter, same as Orion's SET_PARAM. param @16, target (channel or bus id) @17, value @18. Used for: gain (0x50), input_mode (0x4f), phantom (0x51), phase_invert (0x52), bus_level (0x47), bus_mute (0x48), bus_dim (0x66), bus_mono (0x69), param 0x49 (see params).
command.evidence: preamps/capture_preamp_a1_gain_mic.pcapng etc: op 0x13, param 0x50, [17]=0 (preamp A1) / 1 (A2), [18] swept the gain; mode/phantom/phase in the same layout.

global_command.notes: Device-global setter, value at @17 (no channel byte). Used for sample_rate (param 0x03) and clock_source (param 0x04).
global_command.evidence: capture_05_sample_rate...: op 0x12 param 0x03 value 0-6 @17. capture_06_clock_source...: op 0x12 param 0x04 value 0-2 @17.

link_command.status: capture-confirmed for mixer space 3; physical-preamp space partial
link_command.notes: Same shape as Orion: 0xa2 @16, space @17, pair_index @18, enabled @19. Space 3 (mixer) uses a logical pair index within each 16-channel mix, but reserves 16 wire selectors per mix: Mix 1 pair 0 is wire pair 0 and Mix 2 pair 0 is wire pair 16. The isolated mixer-link captures show Mix 1 selectors 0-7 and Mix 2 selectors 16-23. The durable a2 03 write is the link state setter; a2 04 companion writes were seen only for the first two pairs (wire banks 0 and 1). Space 0 (physical preamp link) is assumed by analogy with Orion; not isolated here.
link_command.evidence: capture_dsp / mixer_links/*: op 0x14 param 0xa2 [17]=3, [18] cycling pair indices, [19]=1. mixer_links/mix1_ch1_ch2_linked.pcapng also flips state_report offset 127.

mix_command.notes: The virtual mixer. NOTE this is opcode 0x16 (Orion's mixer is 0x17) and the sub-cmd byte @17 is 0x04 (Orion 0x05); there is NO per-strip send byte. The Zen Go mixer strip is fader + pan + mute + solo: [18]=mix number (0 = Mix 1, 1 = Mix 2), [19]=channel (0-15), [20]=fader raw = dB attenuation 0 (unity) .. 90 (-90 dB), [21]=pan (low 6 bits, 0x20 = centre, ~0x02 = full L, ~0x3e = full R) + mute bit 0x40 + solo bit 0x80. Whole strip state every frame. No 0x73 STATE-REPORT readback -- fader/pan/mute/solo writes produce no state_report change. The in-band 0x74/0x75 cat-0x04 layout for mix indices 0 and 1 is capture-confirmed and decoded by the profile-driven parser; live round-trip still needs hardware verification.
mix_command.evidence: mixer/capture_mixer_09_fader_unlinked...: d4 04 00 01 <fader> 20 sweeping fader. capture_mixer_07_pan...: [21] swept around 0x20. capture_mixer_11_mute: [21] = 0x60 (0x20|0x40) vs 0x20. capture_mixer_13_solo: [21] = 0xa0 (0x20|0x80). capture_08_mixer_volume_faders_on_2_mixes: [18] = 0 and 1, [19] up to 10.

output_command.status: observed -- likely the same mix_command shape addressing a fixed output strip
output_command.notes: The big monitor knob / output volume + mute also go through opcode 0x16 / 0xd4, as d4 04 01 03 <level> <flags> -- i.e. mix index 1, channel 3, with a pan/flags base of 0x02 (not 0x20). [20] = level (0-~0x5a), [21] bit 0x40 = mute. Whether ([18]=1,[19]=3) is a real (mix,channel) address or a special output-strip selector is not pinned down. Buses 0/1/2 have their OWN setter (bus_level 0x47 / bus_mute 0x48 / param 0x66, opcode 0x13) -- see params and 'buses'. Which of these two the Launcher uses for which physical output is not fully mapped.
output_command.evidence: capture_02_volume_down / _03_volume_up: d4 04 01 03 <level> 02 sweeping level. capture_04_mute_toggle: [21] = 0x42 vs 0x02.

routing_command.status: frame + index mapping + source banks DECODED (2026-08-31); destination groups partly decoded
routing_command.notes: Same shape as Orion: [16]=0xd3, [17]=0x41 (=65), [18]=destination group, then an array of (source_bank, source_index) pairs from @19, stride 2, one slot per output channel of the group. Whole group re-sent on any change; no 0x73 STATE-REPORT readback. The Zen Go also answers the in-band 0x74/0x75 readback for the capture-confirmed routing indices 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9; those explicit layouts are the safe bounds used by the WebUI. The 'channel assignments' tab assigns what each MIXER INPUT STRIP listens to. THE SLOT INDEX = MIXER STRIP NUMBER - 1 (slot 0 = strip 1 ... slot 15 = strip 16), confirmed by the index_map_5_8 / 9_12 / 13_16 captures which set slot 4..15 to the oscillator one at a time. Set a slot to (0x08, 0) to mute that strip's input; there is no 'no source'.

destination_groups.3: 8 slots -- mirrors the first 8 slots of dest 6/7/8/9 (changes propagate to both). A 'core'/8-channel view or a separate 8-ch bus; role not pinned down.
destination_groups.5: 4 slots -- mixer strips 1-4 only. dest 3 / 6-9 do NOT track dest 5, so it is a distinct target (best guess: the USB record / direct-monitor input map for the first 4 channels).
destination_groups.6, 7, 8, 9: 32 slots each -- slots 0-15 = the 16 mixer strips, slots 16-31 always MUTE (0x08, unused/reserved). The Launcher ALWAYS writes all four identically and in lockstep (the 'surface_propagation' captures confirm a change to one propagates to all four), so they are one logical map -- the mixer's global strip-input assignment. Per-mix level/pan/mute IS independent (capture_mixer_19); only the input assignment is shared.

source_banks.0x01: computer playback -- idx N = playback channel N+1 (confirmed: 'ch3_cp1' -> (0x01,0), 'ch4_cp2' -> (0x01,1), 'ch5_cp3' -> (0x01,2); default maps use idx up to 7)
source_banks.0x02: S/PDIF in -- idx 0/1 = L/R (from 'ch1-4 - was spdif1,spdif2...': slot 2 was (0x02,1) = spdif R)
source_banks.0x03: UNCONFIRMED -- a 4-channel bank seen only as the DEFAULT source of strips 1-4 in dest 3/6-9 ((0x03,0)..(0x03,3)); no capture ever set a strip TO bank 0x03. Likely computer playback 1-4 via a second tap, or a loopback / mix-return / FX-return bus.
source_banks.0x08: MUTE (pseudo-source, idx 0) -- confirmed by all the '..._mute' captures
source_banks.0x09: oscillator -- idx 0/1 = Osc 1 / Osc 2 (the test-tone source used throughout the index-map captures)
source_banks.0x0a: emumic / mic-modeled preamp -- idx 0/1 (from 'changed ch1 to emu1' -> (0x0a,0))

routing_command.evidence: channel_assignments/*.pcapng and mixer/capture_mixer_03/04/18-30. Each single-strip capture (chN_<src>_oscillator1_<src>) changes exactly one slot and names the source; the index_map captures walk slots 4-15 through the oscillator; capture_mixer_03/04 cycle strip 11 through preamp / playback / emumic / spdif / osc / mute.

observed_opcodes._comment: Opcodes seen in captures but not decoded. Do NOT send these until a client understands them (see family constraints -- an unknown opcode cost a physical power cycle on the Discrete 8 Pro).
observed_opcodes.0x1a: param 0xd5, [17]=8 [18]=5 -- in capture_07_dsp (DSP / FX slot?), 1 frame
observed_opcodes.0x23: param 0xd7, [17]=17 [18]=0 -- in capture_07_dsp, 3 frames (FX bypass / param?)

offset_convention.notes: Scalar state offsets below index the full 320-byte 0x73 frame. candidate_preamp_meters.offset and meter_mappings.payload_offset index the 0x73 snapshot payload after the 0x10-byte frame header. The two coordinate systems describe the same bytes; do not subtract 0x10 from the existing scalar offsets.

output_state.mode_encoding: exclusive observed enum; no capture combines mute and dim
output_state.evidence: zen-go-tui/docs/protocol/zengosc-capture-audit.md: the isolated output controls identify payload 0x0c/0x0e/0x10 as Monitor/HP1/HP2 levels and payload 0x0d/0x0f/0x11 as their mode bytes.

preamp_cluster.notes: The active gain byte follows the selected input mode. Settled mode-switch captures preserve separate stored gains per input and mode; a flat gain field is therefore an active-mode view, not the complete stored-gain matrix.
preamp_cluster.evidence: zen-go-tui/docs/protocol/zengosc-capture-audit.md and preamp-protocol.md: the four-byte cluster is isolated at payload 0x18..0x1b, with mode/phantom/phase flags in the status bytes.

surface_selector.evidence: zen-go-tui/docs/protocol/zengosc-capture-audit.md: SET_PARAM 0x49 writes 0x0f/0x0c select the front-panel mixer surface, and snapshot payload 0x6a follows the selection.

mixer_strip_meters.notes: Shared dynamic mixer-strip lanes confirmed by isolated ch1..ch16 captures. These lanes are indexed by mixer strip, not owned by physical inputs or physical outputs; no exact dB calibration is claimed.
mixer_strip_meters.evidence: zen-go-tui/docs/protocol/zengosc-capture-audit.md: payload 0x8e..0x9d maps CHN to lane N-1; idle raw 0x60 is the no-signal end of the inverted scale.

candidate_preamp_meters.evidence: zen-go-tui/docs/protocol/zengosc-capture-audit.md: candidate preamp lanes at payload 0xce/0xcf are accepted only as mixed-signal provisional fields.
zen-go-tui/docs/protocol/zengosc-capture-audit.md: candidate preamp lanes at payload 0xce/0xcf are accepted only as mixed-signal provisional fields.

User-approved provisional assignment of full-report byte 0xeb to Monitor right; this lane is read independently and the output meter feed and stage are unknown.
User-approved provisional assignment of full-report byte 0xec to HP1 left; output meter feed and stage are unknown.
User-approved provisional assignment of full-report byte 0xed to HP1 right; this lane is read independently and the output meter feed and stage are unknown.
User-approved provisional assignment of full-report byte 0xee to HP2 left; output meter feed and stage are unknown.
User-approved provisional assignment of full-report byte 0xef to HP2 right; this lane is read independently and the output meter feed and stage are unknown.

bus_block.status_bits_note: No independent mute/dim masks are claimed for this capture dialect; status_values is authoritative and the enum values are exclusive in the isolated captures.
bus_block.status_encoding: exclusive observed enum; do not combine codes
bus_block.notes: Zen Go uses the same two-byte-per-bus state layout as its legacy flat fields above. The status byte is an enum, not independent Orion-style bit flags: 0 = normal, 1 = mute, 2 = dim. Mono has no confirmed state-report value yet.

state_report.status: confirmed for gain / mode / phantom / phase / sample_rate / clock / bus; other offsets unmapped
state_report.notes: Continuous state report, ~4 ms. Header: [4-5] = 0x0140 (report size). Confirmed readback fields: [18] = sample-rate index (0-6, tracks the SET value ~immediately); [19] = clock-source index (0-2); [40] + channel = active-mode preamp gain (2 channels, A1 @40, A2 @41), same 'raw = dB-ish' scale as Orion, mode-dependent range (mic 0-65, line small, Hi-Z ~0-45); [42] + channel = preamp status byte (input_mode bits 0-1, phantom bit 0x10, phase bit 0x40); [28] + 2*bus = bus block (byte 0 = level 0-96, byte 1 = exclusive output mode enum: 0 normal, 1 mute, 2 dim). Payload 0x0c/0x18/0x6a/0x8e are documented above with their full-report equivalents. [17]/[19] also show a ~3 s connect blip like Orion (17: 0x08->0x00) -- but [19] is ALSO the clock source, so only the [17] change is pure noise. Offsets ~90/126/127 move on mixer-link writes or other mixer state; offset 122 is the confirmed 0x49 surface selector. The 16 mixer-strip meter lanes at payload 0x8e..0x9d are dynamic and rest near 0x60 when idle; the 0xce/0xcf preamp lanes remain provisional mixed-signal candidates. [21-24] carry a sample-rate-derived clock word (moves with rate, like Orion @21-23).

meter_report.notes: The per-channel meter report -- magic 0x83 (Orion uses 0x75 for this; on the Zen Go 0x75 is instead the connect-time NAME/topology report). Resting values ~0x60 (96), drop toward 0 with signal, same inverted scale as Orion's meter. Header [4-5] = 0x0140. Byte-to-channel mapping not worked out.
meter_report.evidence: capture_09_idle_polling.pcapng: 0x83 frames 1:1 with 0x73; metering/ch1.pcapng..ch16.pcapng exercise one channel each (not yet diffed).

readback.status: CONFIRMED PRESENT 2026-09-01 -- the Zen Go speaks the SAME in-band readback protocol as the Orion Studio III (frame.readback there, PROTOCOL.md 4a), byte-for-byte identical request and response headers. Re-analysed from capture_01_enumeration.pcapng after the protocol was decoded on the Orion. This block replaces the old 'name_report' entry, which described the 0x75 frames as a Zen-Go-specific 'connect-time NAME/topology report' -- they are not: they are ordinary readback RESPONSES, and the ASCII was simply category 0x01 (device name + serial + firmware), the same category that carries it on the Orion.
readback.discriminator_note: On the Orion the discriminator matters because its METER report is also magic 0x75 (byte 1 = 0x1f). On the Zen Go the meter is magic 0x83 instead, so 0x75 is unambiguous here -- but the byte-1 check is kept so the same code path serves both devices.

categories.0x00: device id / firmware -- 2 bytes, observed `01 5a`. Orion's 0x00 is an ASCII firmware string ('4.41'); the Zen Go's is binary and NOT yet decoded (0x5a = 90; do not assume a version until confirmed).
categories.0x01: device name + serial + firmware revision -- 48 bytes, ASCII 'Zen Go Synergy C...' then the unit SERIAL then the fw rev. CONTAINS THE DEVICE SERIAL: never paste a raw dump of this category into the repo, an issue, or a capture that gets committed.
categories.0x03: routing / mixer-input assignment readback. This profile's capture-confirmed routing layouts cover indices 3, 5, and 6-9; body variants are documented in capture_dialect_variants below.
categories.0x04: mixer surface state. Indices 0 and 1 each return 16 two-byte strip records (fader level plus pan/mute/solo flags) in the capture dialect used by the profile.
categories.0x0b: mixer-link selector state. The capture-confirmed index 3 response is a 24-byte bitmap: byte N is nonzero when wire selector N is linked; selectors 0-7 belong to Mix 1 and 16-23 to Mix 2.
categories.0x11: 1 byte, observed `02`. Orion's 0x11 is 'S/PDIF + a capability bitmask'; the Zen Go has S/PDIF, so `02` is plausibly a channel/capability count -- UNCONFIRMED, do not rely on it.
categories.0x18: observed dual-surface mixer records at index 0. Only the solo field is declared by the profile; the remaining bytes and exact role are not decoded.

readback.observed_walk: The Zen Go Launcher's connect walk is TINY compared to the Orion's: only 3 queries, categories 0x00 / 0x01 / 0x11, each at index 0 (identical in capture_01_enumeration.pcapng and capture_01_enumeration_diff_filter.pcapng). The Orion walks 113 records across 10 categories. So this capture gives us NO record counts for any category.
readback.hazard: !! COMPLETE CATEGORY COUNTS ARE NOT KNOWN FOR THIS DEVICE. !! On the Orion, an out-of-range readback index crashes the firmware outright (Cortex-M BusFault, physical power cycle required -- see orion_studio_sc.json frame.readback.hazard). The Zen Go is the same protocol family and must be assumed to share the flaw. Its connect walk queries only index 0 of three categories, so `category_counts` remains EMPTY. The WebUI may use only the explicitly capture-confirmed feature layouts (routing cat 0x03 indices 3, 5, 6-9; mixer cat 0x04 indices 0-1; link bitmap cat 0x0b index 3); all other indices remain blocked until bounded by device evidence.

identity._comment: LAYOUT ONLY -- the serial VALUE is never stored in this repo. It is read from the hardware on request (CLI `identity --serial`). Same record shape on the Orion Studio III and the Zen Go Synergy Core, so it is probably family-wide.
identity.notes: Category 0x01 is a 48-byte record of NUL-terminated ASCII at fixed offsets: model name @0, SERIAL @20 (13 chars), hardware revision @36, then 4 binary bytes @44 (little-endian u32; both units seen decode to mid-2021, so plausibly a build/calibration timestamp -- a GUESS, not confirmed). Category 0x00 is a separate record: only 2 bytes here and BINARY (`01 5a`), with no version string -- firmware_offset is null so parse_firmware_record returns None rather than inventing a version. The ASCII fw rev for this device is the '6.6' at offset 36 of category 0x01. Parsed by protocol.parse_identity_record / parse_firmware_record.

layouts.evidence: zen-go-tui/docs/protocol/zengosc-capture-audit.md: isolated mixer-link captures query 0x0b/0x03 and return one byte per selector; a nonzero byte means linked.

record_layouts.name: Zen Go mixer selector links
record_layouts.evidence: zen-go-tui/docs/protocol/zengosc-capture-audit.md: q0b/03 is a 24-byte selector bitmap; byte N is asserted/nonzero when selector N is linked.

zen_go_assignment_readback.notes: The TUI audit also records q03 assignment replies with body[0] as a sub-id: q03/05 is a 9-byte body containing four pairs, while q03/06..09 are 33-byte bodies containing an eight-byte early-bank prefix followed by twelve pairs. This is an alternate capture-dialect shape, not a replacement for this profile's 17/65-byte routing layouts. Do not merge the variants without a response discriminator or fixture; the shared parser currently uses the capture-confirmed routing layouts above.

readback.category_counts_note: Deliberately empty -- see .hazard. Fill this in ONLY from the device's own connect enumeration, never by probing and never by copying the Orion's counts (different device, different record arrays). The routing feature uses only the explicit capture-confirmed layouts above; it does not treat the six observed routing records as a complete category bound. The q0b/03 link bitmap is a bounded feature layout, not proof of the category's complete record count.
readback.cli: Works with the shared code: protocol.build_readback_query / is_readback_response / readback_body; CLI `readback <cat> [idx]`. Routing cat 0x03 indices 3, 5, and 6-9 are capture-confirmed and safely mapped. parse_routing_record uses the profile destination channel counts; parse_mixer_record uses the capture-confirmed Zen Go mixer_state layout for cat 0x04 indices 0 and 1; the generic record decoder exposes the q0b/03 mixer link bitmap.
readback.still_unknown: The exact roles of routing destinations 3 and 5, the complete Zen Go category-0x03 record count, and the discriminator needed to select the alternate q03 assignment body variant remain unknown. Destinations 6-9 are confirmed as one logical 32-slot mixer input map and are written in lockstep. The mixer category 0x04 layouts for indices 0 and 1 and the q0b/03 link bitmap are capture-confirmed; live control round-trip still needs hardware verification.

channels.notes: 2 combo preamps. input_mode via param 0x4f (0 mic / 1 line / 2 hiz). Gain range is mode-dependent (param 0x50): mic 0-65, line approximately -6..20, Hi-Z ~0-45 -- exact rails were not always swept. Captures show separate stored gains per input/mode; readback gain @40+ch is the active mode's value. Phantom = 0x51, phase_invert = 0x52. Readback status @42+ch.

buses._comment: Output buses, addressed in frame.command.channel_offset (@17) like a channel but the id means an output. Captured target ids 0/1/2 map to Monitor / HP1 / HP2.
buses.readback: state_report.bus_block_offset (28) + 2*bus_id: byte 0 = level (0-96), byte 1 = exclusive output mode enum (0 normal, 1 mute, 2 dim). Isolated captures did not establish a combined mute+dim encoding.
buses.evidence: capture_11_output_controls_once_change_at_a_time.pcapng: isolated Monitor / HP1 / HP2 controls emitted op 0x13 param 0x47 (level 0-96) / 0x48 (mute 0/1) / 0x66 (0/1) with target ids 0/1/2; state_report offsets 28-33 tracked.

surface_selection.notes: The front-panel surface selector is shared by the mixer tabs: Monitor/HP1 uses 0x0f and HP2 uses 0x0c. This is a UI selection command, not a routing or mixer-strip write.

fader.encoding: raw = dB attenuation below unity: 0 = 0 dB, 90 = -90 dB

mixer.link: SET_LINK space 3, pair_index = mix * 16 + channel // 2 (software-mirrored, like Orion)

link_pair_index.notes: The logical pair index is channel // 2 within each 16-channel mix. The wire selector reserves 16 values per mix: Mix 1 pair 0 is 0, Mix 2 pair 0 is 16. Isolated captures cover all eight pairs per mix (selectors 0-7 and 16-23). The companion a2 04 write appears only for the first two pairs and is not needed to describe the durable a2 03 link state.
link_pair_index.evidence: mixer_links/mix1_ch1_ch2_linked.pcapng and mix1_ch11_ch12_linked.pcapng emit pair 0 and 5; the matching Mix 2 captures emit pair 16 and 21.

link_readback.notes: A complete q0b/03 response is required before replacing local link state. Bytes 0-7 map to Mix 1 pairs 0-7; bytes 16-23 map to Mix 2 pairs 0-7; bytes 8-15 are not used by the two visible Zen Go mixer surfaces.

input_routing.notes: The four 32-slot destination records are one logical mixer input map. Slots 0-15 correspond to the 16 mixer strips and slots 16-31 are reserved MUTE; the Launcher writes destinations 6, 7, 8, and 9 identically in lockstep.

mixer.readback: No fader/pan/mute/solo changes appear in the 0x73 STATE REPORT. The in-band 0x74/0x75 category 0x04 layout for Mix 1 and Mix 2 is capture-confirmed (16 two-byte fader + pan/flags slots per mix), and q0b/03 is a capture-confirmed 24-byte mixer-link selector bitmap. Live round-trip on this profile remains to be checked.
mixer.notes: 2 mixes ('Mix 1' / 'Mix 2'), 16 input strips each and no separate master strip. Each strip = fader + pan + mute + solo (no send). See frame.mix_command. What each strip's input is comes from the 'channel assignments' routing (frame.routing_command).

gain.notes: Mode-dependent range, same idea as Orion. The line sweep is approximately raw -6..20 and the Hi-Z sweep is approximately 0..45; captures did not always reach the rail. Mode-switch captures show separate stored gains per input/mode, while state_report.gain_base_offset exposes only the active mode's gain.

input_mode.evidence: preamps/capture_preamp_a1_gain_line.pcapng starts with 4f 00 01; _a1_gain_hiz with 4f 00 02; state_report offset 42 tracked 0/1/2.

phantom.constraint: mic mode only (Launcher hides it otherwise)
phantom.evidence: preamps/capture_preamp_a1_mode_phantom.pcapng; capture_07_dsp.pcapng showed state_report offset 43 (channel 1) gain bit 0x10 set.

phase_invert.evidence: preamps/capture_preamp_a1_phase.pcapng: 52 00 01 / 52 00 00 toggled; zen-go-tui/docs/protocol/zengosc-capture-audit.md confirms the 0x40 phase bit in the 0x18..0x1b preamp cluster.

bus_level.encoding: raw = dB attenuation below unity: 0 = 0 dB, 96 = -96 dB

bus_mute.readback: state_report bus_block status byte (offset 29 + 2*bus_id), exact value 1 means mute

bus_dim.readback: state_report bus_block status byte (offset 29 + 2*bus_id), exact value 2 means dim
bus_dim.notes: Per-bus output dim toggle alongside level (0x47) and mute (0x48). The captured command uses the confirmed SET_PARAM frame with bus id @17 and enabled state @18.
bus_dim.evidence: capture_11_output_controls_once_change_at_a_time.pcapng: op 0x13 param 0x66 [17] = 0/1/2, [18] = 0/1; the state report bus flags track the output control state at offsets 29, 31, and 33.

bus_mono.status: candidate (shared family id; Zen Go command not isolated)
bus_mono.notes: The WebUI can now emit the family-shared Mono setter so it no longer fails with an absent-profile-param error. Zen Go has not yet yielded a mono-specific capture or a dedicated state-report value; the output status enum currently reports only normal, mute, and dim.
bus_mono.evidence: Param id 0x69 is confirmed for bus_mono on the Orion and carried as a candidate on the Discrete 8 Pro; Zen Go still needs a mono-only capture for confirmation.

param_0x49.notes: The Zen Go uses 0x49 to select the front-panel mixer surface: 0x0f selects Monitor/HP1 and 0x0c selects HP2. This is a UI surface selector, not a mixer-strip setting or a solo mask. Do not confuse it with Orion's connect-handshake use of the same family parameter id.

sample_rate.values_note: Hz mapping carried from Orion (same opcode 0x12 / param 0x03). Zen Go idle report shows 44100 (0xAC44) as the active rate; the capture name confirms 48/32/44.1 were exercised with 44.1 the default. Index-to-Hz not individually re-verified for all 7.
sample_rate.evidence: capture_05_sample_rate_in_the_end_48_32_44.1_44.1default.pcapng: op 0x12 param 0x03 value 1..6..0, offset 18 followed 1:1; offsets 21-24 carry a rate-derived clock word.

clock_source.values_note: Zen Go exposes exactly 3 clock sources: 0 = Internal, 1 = S/PDIF, 2 = USB. Raw 0 is the internal-clock value used for sample-rate gating.
clock_source.evidence: capture_06_clock_source_no_word_clock_exists.pcapng: op 0x12 param 0x04 values 0/1/2/0 and offset 19 followed 1:1; the capture-derived project clock-source map and the existing antelope-protocol ClockSource code/label mapping both identify 0=Internal, 1=S/PDIF, 2=USB.

mix_pan.encoding: raw = 32 (centre) + degrees; ~0x02 full L, ~0x3e full R

mix_link.frame: link_command (opcode 0x14 / 0xa2) space 3, logical pair_index = channel // 2; wire pair_index = mix * 16 + logical pair_index
mix_link.readback: frame.readback category 0x0b index 3: 24 one-byte selector flags; selector N is linked when its byte is nonzero (Mix 1 selectors 0-7, Mix 2 selectors 16-23)
mix_link.notes: The durable a2 03 setter and q0b/03 bitmap are capture-confirmed. Software is mirrored like every other link in this family: while linked the Launcher re-sends both strips. The state_report byte near offset 127 is incidental/secondary state and is not the authoritative link readback.

family_notes._comment: Antelope Synergy Core HID protocol family. Shared: magic 0x70 command / opcode @4 / param_id @16 / 320-byte reports / EP 0x01 OUT + 0x82 IN on HID interface 3. Param IDs are largely shared (0x50 gain, 0x4f mode, 0x51 phantom, 0x52 phase, 0x47/0x48 bus, 0x12/0x03 sample rate, 0x14/0xa2 link, 0x53/0xd3 routing). NOT shared / device-specific: report magics (Zen Go meter = 0x83, Orion = 0x75; Zen Go 0x75 = name report), the mixer opcode + shape (Zen Go 0x16/0xd4/subcmd 0x04, no send; Orion 0x17/0xd4/subcmd 0x05, has send), state-report offsets, channel/bus counts, source-bank numbers (Zen Go mute = 0x08, osc = 0x09, emumic = 0x0a; Orion mute = 0x0b, osc = 0x0c, emumic = 0x01).
siblings: profiles/orion_studio_sc.json (Orion Studio III, pid 0xa221) -- the reference, richest profile
carried_hazards: An unrecognised opcode cost a physical power cycle on the Discrete 8 Pro, and a 0x61 'unknown opcode' error frame exists in the family -- do NOT send frame.observed_opcodes or any opcode not in constraints.allowed_opcodes.
An out-of-range channel/bus index BusFaulted a Discrete 8 Pro -- validate targets before writing.
Discrete 8 Pro HID report descriptor has no Report ID, so Linux hidraw writes are 321 bytes (leading 0x00 + 320 payload). Check the Zen Go's descriptor before writing from Linux.
min write interval ~250 ms on Discrete 8 Pro (Orion tolerates ~30-80 ms); unknown for Zen Go -- rate-limit.

constraints._comment: Bounds a client should enforce before writing. Conservative first pass -- widen only as captures confirm.
constraints.allowed_opcodes_note: 0x16 (SET_MIX) and 0x53 (SET_ROUTE) are frame-decoded but NOT hardware round-trip tested from this project. 0x1a / 0x1c / 0x23 (DSP) are observed-only and excluded on purpose.
constraints.gain_bounds_note: All Zen Go bounds are conservative/approximate because the captures did not always sweep to the rail; line -6..20 is the observed signed range, Hi-Z is approximately 0..45, and mic 0..65 comes from the A1/A2 mic-gain sweeps.
constraints.value_from_user_input: never send a raw value straight from user input; clamp to the documented range
